description: Figure 3 is a circular, two-ring donut chart intended to show how inter-annotator agreement is distributed across levels of sample-level ambiguity, with the outer ring representing “Ambiguity Std (Outer)” and the inner ring representing “Max Ambiguity (Inner).” The figure does not use Cartesian axes; instead, categories are encoded as colored arc segments around the circle, with a legend on the right listing the category labels and their corresponding shades of blue. In the outer ring (Ambiguity Std), four blue segments are labeled with percentages: “Std: 0.0” is the largest segment at approximately 47.7%, “Std: 0.47” is about 19.0%, “Std: 0.82” is about 14.2%, and “Std: 0.94” is the smallest at about 7.0%. In the inner ring (Max Ambiguity), three lighter-blue segments are labeled: “Max: 1” is about 38.0%, “Max: 2” is about 39.0%, and “Max: 3” is about 5.0%. The segments appear arranged around the circle without an explicitly stated sorting rule, and no slices are visually emphasized beyond the use of distinct color shades and embedded percentage labels.
